claims.text: Controlled aging or annealing induces nanoscale, stable intermetallic precipitates in the high-entropy alloy.
The resulting intermetallic precipitates will be homogeneously distributed in the alloy matrix.
The intermetallic precipitates obstruct dislocation motion.
The intermetallic precipitates obstruct sub-grain boundary sliding.
Obstruction of dislocation motion enhances mechanical durability.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and sub-grain boundary sliding improves room-temperature creep resistance.
The intermetallic precipitates contribute to the formation of protective passive films.
The precipitate-associated passive films improve corrosion resistance.
The aged alloy will have statistically significantly higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit less room-temperature creep deformation under constant load than the as-cast baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit a more noble corrosion potential than the as-cast baseline.
The aged alloy will exhibit a lower corrosion current density than the as-cast baseline.
Non-oxidizing conditions and precisely controlled temperature and time can promote precipitate nucleation and growth without excessive coarsening.
The beneficial effects require an alloy composition within an optimal range for precipitate formation.
Insufficient or excessive precipitate growth will diminish the predicted improvements.
